skill.name: product-demand-evidence
skill.description: Review public posts and comments for evidence about a product idea and its intended audience. Use supplied material or search supported platforms through SocialDataX.
skill.summary: Create a sourced product demand brief that separates supporting evidence, counterevidence, and questions still to test.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: Most scanner alerts reflect Markdown or readable Chinese text, but the workflow runs an unpinned CLI that accesses runtime credentials. Online research can send task data to a paid provider, and shared Xiaohongshu links must retain their tokens. No evidence of embedded secrets, obfuscated payloads, or prompt injection targeting the audit was found.

remediation.issue: The documented CLI commands run a mutable package release without an install prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Pin and verify the CLI package and its dependencies. Require approval before installing or running it with access to credentials.

remediation.issue: The CLI reads environment credentials and can persist a key in a local JSON file.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer an OS credential store or scoped runtime injection. Verify file permissions when local storage is necessary and keep credential access isolated from unrelated secrets.

remediation.issue: Shell examples use placeholders for user and provider data without specifying safe argument handling.
remediation.suggestion: Use a structured tool or pass keywords and URLs as separate process arguments without a shell. Treat returned links and share text as untrusted input.

remediation.issue: The online workflow lacks a per-task confirmation step for external data transfer and paid calls.
remediation.suggestion: Show the destination, proposed query data, and request budget before online use. Require user confirmation and offer an offline option.

remediation.issue: The skill prohibits redacting Xiaohongshu link tokens in reports and forwarded copies.
remediation.suggestion: Use note IDs or verified token-free citations in shared reports. Keep full links only where retrieval requires them, and do not log or forward them by default.

content.user_title: Evaluate Product Demand with Public Evidence
content.value_statement: Public discussions can reveal unmet needs, but repeated complaints and popular posts can overstate demand. Build a sourced brief that separates pain points, alternatives, purchase concerns, and counterevidence.
actual_capabilities: Analyze supplied posts and comments without network access or an API key.
Search Xiaohongshu, Douyin, or Baidu Tieba through SocialDataX and retrieve selected post details and top-level comments.
Track search coverage, source links, dates, and gaps. Deduplicate entries by platform and source identifier.
Group sourced quotes by pain point, workaround, buying concern, or evidence against the idea.
Distinguish evidence that matches the target audience from evidence about related audiences.
Suggest up to three interviews or small tests for unanswered questions.
limitations: Default research covers at most two platforms, with two one-page searches per platform and up to four posts for detailed review.
Online research uses authenticated SocialDataX access, sends research inputs to the provider, and may incur charges.
The workflow does not post, message users, recruit participants, or monitor discussions automatically.
The sample cannot establish market size, paid conversion, or product success.

use_cases.title: Test an early product idea
use_cases.description: Review complaints, current alternatives, and buying concerns before choosing which product assumption to test.

use_cases.title: Prepare customer interviews
use_cases.description: Use sourced comments to identify unclear needs and draft interview questions about current behavior.

use_cases.title: Compare requests with current workarounds
use_cases.description: Check whether a proposed feature solves a recurring problem or whether existing tools already meet the need.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize pasted feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only these posts and comments: [material]. For [audience], list the main pain points and quote one source for each. Do not search online.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have a small set of comments and need a first pass.

prompt_templates.title: Compare alternatives and objections
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [sources] for [audience] considering [product idea]. Separate manual workarounds, paid alternatives, and objections. Note where the material does not establish buying intent.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to understand why people keep their current approach.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a bounded platform search
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan SocialDataX searches on Xiaohongshu and Baidu Tieba for [idea] among [audience]. Show the proposed queries and limits before searching. Wait for my approval before any online calls.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need new evidence and want to review what will be sent to the provider.

prompt_templates.title: Test a product assumption
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [sources], assess whether [audience] would replace [alternative] with [idea]. Deduplicate evidence, separate audience matches, and list counterexamples. Propose up to three tests for the biggest uncertainties.
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a decision brief for a specific assumption.

output_examples.input: Use these supplied comments to assess whether freelance designers need an invoice reminder tool.
output: Illustrative coverage: Five supplied comments, four distinct entries after deduplication.
Pain point: One freelancer said, "I forget until the payment is already late" (Comment 2).
Alternative: Another freelancer said calendar reminders already work (Comment 4).
Assessment: The sample shows a follow-up problem but does not show willingness to pay.
Next step: Ask freelancers to demonstrate how they track their most recent unpaid invoice.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a shared shopping list would help households that already use group chat.
output: Illustrative coverage: Three supplied discussions. One explicitly mentioned the target household setup.
Supporting evidence: A participant said, "The list gets buried in the chat" (Discussion 1).
Counterevidence: A participant in a related household said pinned messages were enough (Discussion 3).
Next step: Compare a pinned message with a shared list during one shopping trip.

best_practices: Name the audience, the problem, and the product assumption before collecting evidence.
Look for people who are satisfied with existing alternatives as well as people asking for help.
Review which keywords and links would go to SocialDataX before approving online research.
anti_patterns: Treating likes, views, or comment totals as counts of interested buyers.
Counting duplicate comments, repeated stories, or promotions as independent evidence.
Treating help requests or complaints about price as proof of willingness to pay.

faq.question: Can I use this without an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the original posts or comments and ask for offline analysis. Live searches require an authenticated SocialDataX CLI or an existing authenticated MCP connection.

faq.question: Which platforms can it search?
faq.answer: It supports Xiaohongshu, Douyin, and Baidu Tieba through SocialDataX. The default is Xiaohongshu and Baidu Tieba, with Douyin as an option for video-focused research.

faq.question: What does SocialDataX receive?
faq.answer: Live requests send research keywords, links, and identifiers to SocialDataX. Use supplied material offline when the idea or sources should stay private.

faq.question: Are online searches free?
faq.answer: Online calls are billed by SocialDataX. The documented CLI credential status check does not call a paid endpoint.

faq.question: What happens when a search fails or finds little?
faq.answer: The brief keeps the evidence already gathered and notes the missing coverage. It does not silently expand the search or invent examples.

faq.question: Can this tell me how large the market is?
faq.answer: No. The brief describes what the sample supports and what remains uncertain. It does not estimate market size or predict sales.
